summary: Mrs. Mizrachi discusses the historical experiences of Sephardic Jews following their expulsion from Spain, focusing on the rise of the Inquisition and the subsequent diaspora into the Ottoman Empire. She highlights the influential roles of Donna Gracia and Joseph Hanassi in establishing economic networks and supporting Jewish settlement in the Land of Israel, including Tiberias and Safed. The class examines how these historical figures and communities contributed to the development of the old Yeshuv and the preservation of Sephardic identity.
questions: How did the Inquisition change the way Jewish identity was perceived in Spain?
What role did Donna Gracia and Joseph Hanassi play in the Sephardic diaspora?
How did the Ottoman Empire facilitate the settlement of Sephardic Jews in the Land of Israel?
What is the connection between the Sephardic diaspora and the development of the old Yeshuv?
Why does Mrs. Mizrachi argue that the history of the old Yeshuv is often overlooked in modern narratives?
